chose: the ambiguous case exists but did not arise; conservation holds and attribution stayed unforced
because: Replayed hoist's real extraction against the pre-refactor baseline, which is the discriminating test the conjecture named. Two context|expr keys DID carry multiple baselined sites — sql-ident|frame.reference.label at (patient.ts, shared/paths/divergence.ts) and sql-ident|u.characteristic at (patient.ts, shared/paths/schemas.ts) — so the ambiguous case is real, not hypothetical. chose: a baseline cannot be CONSTRUCTED without declaring its rename semantics — the omission becomes a compile error, not a default
over: a shared reconcile() implementation across the three ratchets, which would paper over a real semantic difference: sink sites are DISCOVERED so a move should be forgiven, while components are DECLARED so a rename arguably SHOULD be signal
leaving each ratchet to answer independently, which is how we got three schemes and three different answers with nothing forcing the third author to notice there was a question
supplying a safe default (forgive moves everywhere), which trades a loud wrong answer for a quiet one
because: sidecar.ts already owns baseline I/O (readBaseline/writeBaseline) but nothing owns baseline IDENTITY — what counts as the same pinned fact across time. So the question got answered three times, differently, by three authors who never had to notice they were answering it: lint-sinks keyed kind|file|expr (broke on every refactor until v0.20.1), conventions keyed {name,sites} (immune by construction, verified by experiment), mass keys lines|<component> (a rename still reads as vanish+new). Shipping the lint-sinks fix DEEPENED the asymmetry — one ratchet now understands moves and the others do not. The fix is a shared OBLIGATION, not a shared implementation: a baseline type parameterized by an explicit rename policy — forgives-moves | immune-by-key | rename-is-signal — so all three answers stay legal and the omission stops being one. That is the harness's own dissolve>declare>infer applied to itself: today the policy is inferred from whatever the author happened to write; this makes it declared at the type, and the missing declaration unrepresentable
